> 治大國，若烹小鮮.

Chapter 59 said: bring the harvest in.

Chapter 60 gives a heat setting.

## 鮮 is a fresh fish

鮮: 魚名，出貉國 — originally the name of a fish. But in pre-Qin use 鮮 is mostly 新 — new, freshly killed.

So 小鮮 is not "small dried fish." It is the small fish that has just gone into the pan.

It is the most tender and the least tolerant of being turned.

## The instruction is a prohibition

The analogy's whole content is one negative: don't flip it.

A small fresh fish needs the pan to be hot, the time to be right, and then nothing. Every turn breaks it. A large fish can be turned because it has thickness; a large state can absorb a correction because it has reserve. A small fish and a large state that is being governed well are both in a condition where the intervention is the damage.

Note that the analogy does not recommend neglect. The fire is on. The fish is in the pan. What is being withheld is only the flurry.

## 以道蒞天下

蒞: built on 艸 and 位 — the grass and the standing place. To arrive at a position, as one arrives at a post.

So 蒞天下 is not "rule the world" but "take up the position of the world."

## 其鬼不神

The 鬼 do not 神.

神 here is a verb: to display efficacy, to work as a spirit does — to produce effects that command belief.

> 非其鬼不神，其神不傷人.

Not that the ghosts have lost their efficacy; their efficacy no longer harms.

The chapter is careful about causality. The 鬼 are not abolished; the arrangement has changed so that their operation has nowhere to land.

Which is the same structure as chapter 50's 無死地: not invulnerability, but the absence of a surface.

## 非其神不傷人，聖人亦不傷人

Not only does the efficacy not harm — the sage does not harm either.

The two halves are joined by 亦, "also." The chapter puts the sage and the 鬼 on the same ledger, and this is the boldest move in it: the ruler's measures and the uncanny forces are the same category of thing — powers that produce effects by acting on people.

## 夫兩不相傷，故德交歸焉

Two do not harm each other; therefore 德交歸.

交: 交脛也 — the legs crossed.

So 交歸 is not "the virtue is handed back." It is: each yields a leg, and both go home. Two parties walking away from each other, neither having taken the other's ground.

That image is the conclusion of the whole chapter. What the pan needed was not more attention but the absence of contact.

## Why this follows 59

59: the store is full, so there is no deficit to be filled by intervention.
60: so the pan can be left alone. Interference is usually the attempt to supply something that is missing.

Which makes the two chapters one argument: 嗇 builds the reserve, and the reserve is what makes 不翻 possible.

## A test

Take a system that is working — a team, a routine, a piece of writing in progress. Count the last five interventions you made. Then ask which of them were corrections and which were the flinch of someone who needed to be doing something.
